hero.title: From chaos to insights.
hero.sub: One source of truth your whole team trusts, and analysts who get their week back. Built properly, documented fully, handed over completely. AI where it earns its place, governed from day one.

entries.def: The capacity to act. Your data in one trusted place, owned by you and documented for you, so decisions stop waiting on it.
A consulting practice of one architect. Design, build, then a full handover: code, docs, runbooks and keys. Scope, timeline and costs agreed before we start.
Agency with AI built in. One use case at a time, measured before it scales, governed from day one. Not a vibe-coded data strategy.

items.text: Your data lives in 5+ different places and nobody can agree on a single source of truth.
Analysts spend 80% of their time cleaning data instead of actually using it.
You're paying for automations but not getting ROI from your AI & cloud investment.

flow.label: How it works
flow.title: One governed flow, from sources to answers.
flow.sub: This is the medallion architecture we build. Every source lands raw, gets cleaned and tested once, and feeds every dashboard and model from the same governed layer.
flow.caption: Sources land in Bronze exactly as they arrive. Silver cleans, conforms and tests. Gold carries the semantic layer that dashboards and AI read.

lakehouse.caption: One governed store instead of scattered copies. Purview or Dataplex enforces policies and lineage; the semantic layer serves BI and AI from the same numbers.

pipelines.caption: Every run is scheduled, built with dbt and tested before anything reaches Gold. When a test fails, the alert comes to the engineer first, never to your stakeholders.

aidata.caption: The same governed Gold data feeds both classic ML and retrieval for AI. Every feature and every embedding traces back to its source.

governance.caption: AI reaches production one use case at a time, measured before it scales, on a rail of access control, audit logging and human sign-off.
governance.rail: access control · audit log · human sign-off

about.caption: The whole engagement in one line. From the design onward everything lives in your repositories, so the handover is a formality, not a cliff.

work.caption: What every engagement looks like from above: point-to-point connections nobody dares to touch, replaced by one governed flow everyone can read.

items.title: Pipelines & automation
items.desc: Data that is fresh, tested and ready when your team sits down. Built with dbt on BigQuery or Fabric, orchestrated with Airflow or Fabric pipelines, monitored so quality issues surface before your stakeholders do.

items.title: AI-ready data layers

items.desc: AI that reaches production and earns its keep. A phased rollout with security, access control and evaluation built in, from the first use case onward.

Security and access control designed in

handover.label: The deliverables
handover.title: What you keep.
handover.sub: Every engagement ends with a handover, not a renewal conversation. This is what lands in your hands, shown as samples, not staged client work.
handover.cap1: The design, written so anyone on your team can read it.
handover.cap2: Every run tested. A failure alerts the engineer, it never surprises you.
handover.cap3: Runbooks and keys, in repositories you own from the first commit.

process.label: No black boxes
process.title: Audit, design, build, handover. You keep the keys and the docs.

about.title: One architect, end to end.
about.body1: data aigency is the remote practice of Vadim Van Den Heuvel. The person who takes your first call is the person who designs the architecture, builds it and hands it over. No salesperson, no junior team behind the curtain. Every diagram on this site is drawn the way your documentation will be written: so anyone on your team can read it.
about.body2: And nothing depends on me staying. Everything lives in your repositories from the first commit, your tables sit in open formats like Delta and Iceberg, and every decision is documented, so any engineer can pick up where I leave off. Scope, timeline and costs are agreed up front. Full handover of code, docs and runbooks. No lock-in, no black boxes.

contact.title: Let's talk about your data stack.
contact.sub: A free 30 minute intake call. We walk through your current stack, the problems you are running into and the solutions worth considering. You leave with a short written summary, whether we work together or not. No deck, no obligations.
